title: ACC Saturator: Automatic Kernel Optimization for Directive-Based GPU Code
problem: Automatic code optimization typically employs monolithic algorithms that irreversibly modify program structure, requiring repetitive implementation for similar analyses across compilers. Optimizing directive-based GPU code requires exploration of multiple optimization strategies while preserving correctness.
motivation: Efficient GPU kernel optimization is critical for high-performance computing, as simultaneous reduction in computation and memory access with improved memory throughput can significantly improve application performance.
method: The framework uses equality saturation to perform exhaustive term rewriting on directive-based GPU kernels. It constructs single-assignment forms from input code and systematically rewrites them while preserving dependencies. The approach extracts optimal cases by leveraging computational reordering and strategic memory-access ordering to achieve simultaneous improvements across computation, memory access, and throughput.
key_novelty: Applying equality saturation to exhaustively optimize directive-based GPU code through single-assignment form rewriting that simultaneously reduces computation, memory access, and improves memory throughput.
contributions: Adaptation of equality saturation technique for automatic GPU kernel optimization in directive-based programming
Automated framework for constructing and exhaustively rewriting single-assignment forms while preserving code semantics and dependencies
Demonstration of significant performance improvements across multiple compiler backends
Analysis of computational reordering and memory-access ordering criticality for modern GPU performance
